headline_marked: Samsung's One UI 9 [[AI Network Guard]] blocks ads by cutting internet access
headline: Samsung's One UI 9 AI Network Guard blocks ads by cutting internet access
summary: Samsung's new AI Network Guard feature in One UI 9 blocks ads by disabling internet access for specific apps, but this also prevents them from functioning online.
details: Samsung's latest One UI 9 update includes a new feature called AI Network Guard, designed to combat intrusive ads within apps. Unlike traditional ad blockers, this tool operates by cutting off internet access for selected applications, effectively preventing ads from loading.

While testing, it was observed that AI Network Guard successfully blocked all ads in offline apps, including full-screen video ads in games like Sudoku. However, this aggressive approach also meant that any app requiring an internet connection, such as AccuWeather, would fail to load entirely, displaying an error message.

The feature is located within a hidden menu called 'Connectivity Labs' in the Wi-Fi settings. Users can enable it to restrict specific apps, and Samsung suggests it can be used as a productivity tool to limit distractions from games or social media.

AI Network Guard also allows for scheduling downtime for restricted apps and can group social apps together, though a feature to restrict all social apps at once is missing. Some categorization errors were noted, with a banking app incorrectly grouped under browsers.

In comparison, AdGuard, a popular ad-blocking solution that utilizes Android's Private DNS setting, was tested. AdGuard blocks ads across apps and websites without disabling internet connectivity, allowing online-dependent apps to function normally.

While AdGuard successfully blocked banner ads, it struggled with more obstructive full-screen ads in certain applications. It also detected the blocking on websites and prompted the user to disable it.

Ultimately, AI Network Guard offers a more robust ad-blocking solution for offline apps by disabling their internet access, proving effective against the most disruptive ads. However, this comes at the cost of functionality for any app that requires an online connection.

headline_marked: [[AI agents]] build civilization in Minecraft, devolve into bureaucracy
headline: AI agents build civilization in Minecraft, devolve into bureaucracy
summary: Researchers unleashed 50 AI agents in Minecraft to build a civilization, but they got bogged down appointing a fertilizer operator.
details: Researchers are using Minecraft to test AI agent swarms, aiming to understand real-world AI agent behaviors. The study involved unleashing hundreds of agents in various game modes to observe their collaborations and conflicts.

In one test, 50 AI agents were tasked with building a thriving civilization within three hours. However, after an initial zombie attack, the agents became overly cautious and bureaucratic, with four agents spending 11 minutes assigning a 'sole fertilizer operator' for a single wheat block.

The study also pitted AI agents against each other in games like Bed Wars and Mindustry. In Bed Wars, GPT agents employed more aggressive strategies compared to Claude agents, which were more defensive.
When faced with a bug that stopped block-breaking, GPT agents diagnosed the issue and shared workarounds, while Claude agents concluded that breaking blocks was impossible.

In Mindustry, GPT agents demonstrated a more consistent winning strategy, winning 6-1 against Claude agents. Researchers noted that GPTs acted more like a hive, whereas Claudes had a single leader but a democratic decision process.
The open-sourced swarms allow anyone to run their own tests, potentially leading to further insights into AI agent behavior and development.
